historical_references.reference: Gianna Beretta Molla, an Italian doctor and mother, was born on April 4, 1922. She was beatified in 2001 and canonized in 2004 by the Catholic Church. Gianna is remembered for refusing a therapeutic abortion to save her own life, as she was pregnant with her fourth child and suffering from a heart condition that required immediate surgery. She died on April 28, 1962, but her unborn daughter, who was delivered by caesarean section after her death, survived.

Gianna Maria Sassato, an Italian nun and World War II heroine, was born on April 23, 1914, in the village of Campo Ligure, in the province of Genoa. She joined the Order of the Sisters of Mercy and became a teacher. During the war, she was arrested by the Germans and taken to a concentration camp. There, she organized a secret school for the children of other prisoners and taught them in the evenings, risking her own life. She died on November 24, 1943.
